conformantStories.evidence: setDesiredAPY L151-172: first call always previews (apySetInProgress defaults false -> isPreview true L153-155); commit branch requires apySetInProgress && block.number <= pendingAPYBlockNumber+100 && bps==pendingAPYBps; commit runs _updatePool then _updatePhUSDEmissionRate (L165-168) and clears apySetInProgress; a single call never mutates desiredAPYBps; state always progresses (every call either previews or commits). Matches the 'preview->commit, same value within 100 blocks, never lockable' acceptance criteria.

Withdrawn emits actualWithdrawAmount (the dust-adjusted amount, L368 with adjustment at L347-351); Staked emits recipient not msg.sender (L327); RewardsClaimed emits the actual minted/transferred amounts and only when non-zero (L452-453). Matches the 'events fire with the recipient/amount actually applied' acceptance criteria.

The EMA-era explicit same-block guard/lastClaimTimestamp are gone, but _updatePool early-returns when block.timestamp <= lastRewardTime (L390), so accStablePerShare/accPhUSDPerShare cannot increase twice in one block. Same-block collectReward->stake->claim sequences accrue zero per-share within the block. The forbid-same-block-inflation intent is preserved by the Linear-Depletion early-return.

conformantStories.result: FAITHFUL for stake/withdraw/APY-commit paths; DEVIATION on pauseWithdraw path (see F-004)
conformantStories.evidence: _updatePhUSDEmissionRate (L461-470) exactly implements totalStaked*desiredAPYBps/10000/SECONDS_PER_YEAR and returns 0 when totalStaked==0; invoked on stake (L324), withdraw (L365), APY commit (L168). The only enumerated totalStaked-changing op that does NOT refresh the rate is pauseWithdraw -> F-004.

findings.storyTag: foundational 2f678c3 (EMA->Linear Depletion); model named in story-005
alsoAt: collectReward L283 (rewardPerSecond recompute on every push)
findings.specText: 2f678c3 body: replaced EMA smoothing with `rewardPerSecond = rewardBalance / depletionDuration`, "recalculating only when the balance changes (deposits or claims)"; model named "Linear Depletion" whose stated goal is to "pay out rewardBalance evenly over depletionDuration". lib/phlimbo-ea/CLAUDE.md: "Has the V1 rate-recompute bug: rewardPerSecond is recomputed on every stake/withdraw/claim, effectively re-anchoring the depletion window on each user interaction."
findings.specSource: git commit 2f678c3 body + lib/phlimbo-ea/CLAUDE.md (submodule design narrative)
findings.actualBehavior: Inside _updatePool, after every non-zero distribution, line 416 recomputes `rewardPerSecond = rewardBalance * PRECISION / depletionDuration` against the post-distribution (reduced) balance, re-anchoring the full depletion window to `depletionDuration` from `now`. Because this fires on every interaction that distributes (and again on every collectReward and setDepletionDuration), the continuous dynamics are dB/dt = -B/D, i.e. exponential decay B(t)=B0*e^(-t/D), not linear depletion. Stable rewards therefore under-distribute / stall: ~63% paid over one depletionDuration of continuous activity, the residual asymptoting toward (but never reaching) full payout. The realized rate is also path-dependent (frequent interaction = slower payout). Combined with floored per-share crediting (rewardBalance debited in full but accStablePerShare floors), a remainder is also permanently stranded (recoverable only via emergencyTransfer).
findings.deviation: The advertised 'Linear Depletion / even payout over depletionDuration' model is not implemented; the rate is re-anchored on every interaction, producing exponential decay and chronic under-distribution of stable rewards owed to stakers. The mechanism the commit body describes is itself the defect (CLAUDE.md labels it a bug; PhlimboV2 removes the _updatePool recompute).
findings.classification: BOTH a Law-2 faithfulness deviation (implementation contradicts the stated Linear-Depletion model/goal) AND a Law-1 value-impact escalation (stable rewards under-distribute / stall + permanent stranding of stranded remainder). This is the prime PoC target.
findings.knownIssueStatus: Documented as a V1 bug in lib/phlimbo-ea/CLAUDE.md, but NOT present in registered-projects.json known-issues. Per Law 1 (recall beats tidiness) it must be surfaced; the sanitizer should reconcile against the formal known-issues list (CLAUDE.md narrative != registered known-issue).

findings.specText: story-008 HIGH-5 body: "emergencyTransfer(recipient) moves all tokens out and then _pause()s atomically; users get a no-rewards pauseWithdraw(amount) exit usable whenPaused" / "After emergencyTransfer removes all tokens... Users can safely exit via pauseWithdraw()."
findings.specSource: git commit d46506a body (story-008 HIGH-5), relayed in reports/phlimbo-ea-04/audit/story-intents.md L61, L140-150
findings.actualBehavior: emergencyTransfer (L214-227) transfers the ENTIRE phUSD balance (L218-220), which equals totalStaked (all staked principal, INV-2), to `recipient`, then _pause()s. pauseWithdraw (L245-261) decrements user.amount/totalStaked and then does `phUSD.safeTransfer(msg.sender, amount)` (L257). With the contract drained of phUSD, that safeTransfer reverts for every user. The advertised on-chain user-recovery path therefore does NOT exist after an emergencyTransfer.
findings.deviation: The story's stated user-safety guarantee ('users can safely exit via pauseWithdraw() after emergencyTransfer') is not faithfully implemented: post-drain, pauseWithdraw reverts for all users. pauseWithdraw is only coherent after a plain pause() (no drain). The guarantee is mislabelled.
findings.classification: Law-2 faithfulness-only deviation (contradiction between the story's stated recovery guarantee and the implementation). NOT a Law-1 escalation: the drain itself is a knowing owner action (Law 3 trusted) and the intended real-world flow (parent story-049: emergencyTransfer(owner) then off-chain redistribution) routes principal to the trusted owner, so there is no protocol value loss - only a false on-chain-recovery claim. Note the separate LOCAL-006 footgun (pauser==0 permanent-pause) is what would make the missing on-chain path actually harmful.

findings.specText: 7529a45 body (rationale for removing the yieldAccumulator-only restriction): `safeTransferFrom` means the caller funds it; `nonReentrant` added to collectReward. Stated protections: nonReentrant + safeTransferFrom.
findings.specSource: git commit 7529a45 body, relayed in reports/phlimbo-ea-04/audit/story-intents.md L92-94, L152-158
findings.actualBehavior: collectReward is permissionless (L270, no access control) and every call sets `rewardPerSecond = rewardBalance * PRECISION / depletionDuration` (L283), restarting the full depletion window from `now`. Any untrusted caller can push dust to repeatedly re-anchor/re-stretch distribution, slowing stable-reward delivery to existing stakers at cost of only gas + the forfeited dust. The cited protections (nonReentrant, safeTransferFrom) address reentrancy and funding, not this rate-manipulation/window-reset vector. Combined with F-001's per-interaction re-anchoring, an untrusted actor can force the exponential-decay (slow) curve at will.
findings.deviation: The story's safety reasoning (permissionless funding is safe because nonReentrant + safeTransferFrom) is incomplete: it does not cover the depletion-window reset that an untrusted caller can trigger, enabling a griefing / reward-delay vector.
findings.classification: Law-1 escalation of an under-protected story (griefing / value-delay), but LOW severity: no theft, only delay; weak incentive (griefer pays gas indefinitely and forfeits dust); and the root cause is the same rewardPerSecond recompute as F-001 (in normal multi-staker operation the exponential decay already manifests without any griefer). Reported distinctly because it adds an untrusted-triggerable surface that the story claimed was safe.

findings.specText: story-006 body: phUSDPerSecond = (totalStaked * desiredAPYBps) / 10000 / SECONDS_PER_YEAR; "Rate recomputed whenever totalStaked changes (stake/withdraw) and whenever APY changes." Profile INV-7: phUSDPerSecond == totalStaked*desiredAPYBps/10000/SECONDS_PER_YEAR.
findings.specSource: git commit b6044fb body (story-006), relayed in story-intents.md L39-45 + Phlimbo.profile.md INV-7
findings.actualBehavior: pauseWithdraw decrements totalStaked (L254) but does NOT call _updatePhUSDEmissionRate and does NOT advance lastRewardTime. phUSDPerSecond stays sized for the larger pre-pause totalStaked. After unpause, the first _updatePool credits the entire paused interval (timeElapsed = now - frozen lastRewardTime) using the stale (too-high) phUSDPerSecond divided by the now-smaller totalStaked, so remaining stakers earn phUSD at an effective APY above desiredAPYBps. Because phUSD is minted (not balance-backed), this is direct phUSD over-inflation. The stale rate persists until the next stake/withdraw (claim never refreshes it).
findings.deviation: story-006's guarantee that phUSDPerSecond tracks totalStaked (INV-7) is silently regressed by the later HIGH-5 pauseWithdraw, which changes totalStaked without refreshing the emission rate or advancing accrual time -> phUSD over-emission to remaining stakers.
findings.classification: Law-2 faithfulness deviation (later story regressing an earlier story's invariant) WITH value impact (excess phUSD minted = supply inflation). Severity low: only triggers after a pause + pauseWithdraw cycle (requires pauser action and a partial paused exit) and over-emits to honest remaining stakers rather than enabling theft.

findings.storyTag: story-008 HIGH-1 (regressed by story-008 HIGH-5 pauseWithdraw)
findings.specText: story-008 HIGH-1 (29820b2): MINIMUM_STAKE = 1e15 enforced in stake; withdrawal dust prevention forces full withdrawal if remainder < MINIMUM_STAKE. Profile INV-6: every non-zero position >= MINIMUM_STAKE; comment L77 'Minimum stake amount to prevent first depositor attack'.
findings.specSource: git commit 29820b2 body (story-008 HIGH-1), relayed in story-intents.md L52-54 + Phlimbo.profile.md INV-6/LOCAL-005
findings.actualBehavior: pauseWithdraw only checks `user.amount >= amount` (L247) and `amount > 0` (L248); unlike withdraw (L348-351) it applies no dust-forces-full-exit rule, so it can leave 0 < remaining < MINIMUM_STAKE. After unpause these sub-minimum positions persist and totalStaked can fall below MINIMUM_STAKE, weakening the first-depositor / share-inflation mitigation HIGH-1 exists to provide.
findings.deviation: HIGH-1's minimum-position guarantee (INV-6) is weakened by the later HIGH-5 pauseWithdraw, which permits dust residual positions.
findings.classification: Law-2 invariant weakening (later story regressing an earlier story's guarantee). Severity low: the dust positions are the user's own and the first-depositor re-inflation window is narrow; reported for recall/visibility.

notes: No strict [story-NNN] commit governs src/Phlimbo.sol directly; the governing intents are inline-referenced story numbers + untagged foundational commits + lib/phlimbo-ea/CLAUDE.md, per the digest. Acceptance criteria were taken from those sources, not invented.
F-001 is the headline (Law-1 + Law-2). It is documented in submodule CLAUDE.md but absent from registered known-issues, so it survives sanitization (Law 1 recall).
F-003 shares F-001's root cause (rewardPerSecond recompute); dedup may fold it as the permissionless/untrusted-trigger facet.
